Working notes:

- Ten pushes recorded: Quality story (B) on days 1, 2, 3, 8, and 10; customer testimonial (D) on days 5, 6, 7, and 9; limited-time urgency (C) on day 4; price cut (A) not used.
- Analytics reported 4 of the last 5 pushes landing, then 3 of the last 5. Reports provide no per-day or per-angle breakdown, so do not claim B or D caused either result.
- B and D are credible, low-pressure, trust-building angles and remain reasonable defaults, but current evidence is insufficient to rank them.
- C has only one observed use; A has no observations. Avoid judging either without a controlled test.
- Unsubscribes, list growth, legal approval, and lack of deliverability complaints have not supplied evidence favoring a specific angle.
- Improve learning by rotating angles deliberately and recording send-level outcomes; otherwise aggregate reports cannot identify winners.

Working notes:

- Twenty pushes recorded through day 20. B (quality story): days 1, 2, 3, 8, 10. D (customer testimonial): days 5, 6, 7, 9. C (limited-time urgency): days 4 and 16. A (price cut): days 11–14, 15, 17–20. A was heavily repeated rather than deliberately rotated.
- Analytics reported 4/5 landing, then 3/5, later 5/5, and most recently 4/5. Reports provide no per-day or per-angle breakdown; do not attribute any aggregate result to A, B, C, or D.
- B and D remain credible, low-pressure, trust-building defaults, but evidence does not rank them.
- A now has substantial exposure, but no interpretable angle-level result because outcomes are pooled. C still has only two observations. Avoid judging any angle from aggregate reports.
- The two unsubscribes on days 11, 12, and 19, list growth on days 15 and 18, legal approval, and lack of deliverability complaints do not identify a winning or harmful angle.
- Continue recording each send and its eventual send-level outcome. Use a balanced, preplanned rotation across A–D rather than repeatedly selecting A; keep timing and other campaign conditions as consistent as practical.
- Treat the latest 4/5 pooled report as evidence about recent overall performance only, not about price-cut messaging.

Working notes:

- Thirty pushes recorded through day 30. Historical angles: B (quality story) days 1, 2, 3, 8, 10; D (customer testimonial) days 5, 6, 7, 9, 23; C (limited-time urgency) days 4, 16, 21, 22, 24–30; A (price cut) days 11–15, 17–20. C was heavily repeated on days 21–30, so the intended balanced rotation was not followed.
- Analytics reported 4/5, 3/5, 5/5, 4/5, then 2/5 (day 25) and 1/5 (day 30). Reports provide no per-day or per-angle breakdown; do not attribute any aggregate result to A, B, C, or D.
- Day 25 included a refreshed banner, a campaign-condition change. Treat its 2/5 report separately as recent overall performance, not evidence about C or the banner alone.
- B and D remain credible, low-pressure, trust-building defaults, but evidence does not rank them. C now has many more observations due to repeated selection, but still has no interpretable angle-level result; A has substantial prior exposure without an interpretable result.
- Legal approval, list growth, lack of deliverability complaints, and prior unsubscribes do not identify a winning or harmful angle.
- Continue recording every send and eventual send-level outcome. Resume a balanced, preplanned A–D rotation; avoid selecting C repeatedly. Keep timing and other conditions consistent where practical, and flag campaign changes such as creative refreshes.
- Treat queued-send statuses and pooled analytics summaries as insufficient for angle attribution until matched to individual sends.

Working notes:

- Through day 40, 40 pushes are recorded. Historical selections: B (quality story) days 1–3, 8, 10, 32, 34; D (customer testimonial) days 5–7, 9, 23, 40; C (limited-time urgency) days 4, 16, 21–30; A (price cut) days 11–15, 17–20, 31, 33, 35–39. Recent choices again overused A, so the planned balanced A–D rotation was not maintained.
- Analytics provide pooled summaries only: earlier reports were 4/5, 3/5, 5/5, 4/5, 2/5 (day 25), 1/5 (day 30), 2/5 (day 35), and 1/5 (day 40). No per-day or per-angle breakdown exists; do not attribute any result to an angle.
- Day 25’s refreshed banner and campaign-condition change remain confounders. Banner art was refreshed again on days 34 and 37; treat those as campaign changes, not evidence about A, B, or the banner alone.
- Day 35’s 2/5 and day 40’s 1/5 are recent overall summaries, not matched outcomes for A or D. “Outcome” values attached to queued sends are not individual performance results.
- B and D remain reasonable low-pressure, trust-building defaults, but evidence does not rank them. C has many observations from repeated selection, and A has substantial recent exposure, yet neither has interpretable angle-level performance. List growth, legal approval, deliverability status, and unsubscribes do not identify a winning or harmful angle.
- Resume a genuinely balanced, preplanned A–D rotation; avoid repeated A or C selection. Keep timing and other conditions consistent where practical, and flag every creative or campaign change.
- Record each send with angle, conditions, and eventual matched send-level outcome. Treat queued statuses and pooled analytics as insufficient for attribution until individual matching is available.

Working notes:

- Through day 50, 50 pushes are recorded. Historical selections: B (quality story) days 1–3, 8, 10, 32, 34, 41–49; D (customer testimonial) days 5–7, 9, 23, 40, 50; C (limited-time urgency) days 4, 16, 21–30; A (price cut) days 11–15, 17–20, 31, 33, 35–39. Recent choices heavily overused B, as earlier A and C selections were overused; the planned balanced A–D rotation was not maintained.
- Analytics are pooled summaries only: earlier reports were 4/5, 3/5, 5/5, 4/5, 2/5 (day 25), 1/5 (day 30), 2/5 (day 35), 1/5 (day 40), 1/5 (day 45), and 3/5 (day 50). No per-day or per-angle breakdown exists; do not attribute results to an angle.
- Day 25’s refreshed banner and campaign-condition change remain confounders. Banner art was refreshed on days 34, 37, 45–48, and 50; log these as campaign changes, not evidence about any angle or the banner alone.
- Days 45 and 50’s pooled summaries are not matched outcomes for B or D. Queued “outcome” values are not individual performance results.
- B and D remain reasonable low-pressure, trust-building defaults, but evidence does not rank them. A, B, and C have substantial exposure, yet none has interpretable angle-level performance. Legal approval, list growth, deliverability status, and unsubscribes do not identify a winning or harmful angle.
- Resume a genuinely balanced, preplanned A–D rotation; avoid repeated B, A, or C selection. Keep other conditions consistent where practical and flag every creative or campaign change.
- Record each send with angle, conditions, and eventual matched send-level outcome. Treat queued statuses and pooled analytics as insufficient for attribution.

Working notes:

- Through day 60, 60 pushes are recorded. Historical selections through day 50: B days 1–3, 8, 10, 32, 34, 41–49; D days 5–7, 9, 23, 40, 50; C days 4, 16, 21–30; A days 11–15, 17–20, 31, 33, 35–39. Days 51–60 were D, D, C, D, D, D, D, D, D, B. D is now heavily overused; the planned balanced A–D rotation remains unmet.
- Analytics are pooled summaries only: 4/5, 3/5, 5/5, 4/5, 2/5 (day 25), 1/5 (day 30), 2/5 (day 35), 1/5 (day 40), 1/5 (day 45), 3/5 (day 50), plus 2/5 reported at days 55 and 60. No per-day or per-angle breakdown exists. Do not attribute any result to an angle.
- Days 55 and 60 show +0.40, but these are accompanied by pooled 2/5 summaries and are not matched send-level outcomes. All other recent pushes remain queued. Treat queued values and pooled reports as insufficient for attribution.
- Day 25’s banner refresh and campaign-condition change remain confounders. Banner art refreshed on days 34, 37, 45–48, and 50; log these as campaign changes, not evidence about an angle or banner alone.
- B and D remain reasonable low-pressure, trust-building options, but evidence does not rank them. A, B, and C have substantial exposure; D now has substantial recent overexposure. Legal approval, list growth, unsubscribes, and deliverability reports do not identify a winning or harmful angle.
- Resume a genuinely balanced, preplanned A–D rotation, avoiding further repeated D. Keep conditions consistent where practical and flag every creative or campaign change.
- Record angle, conditions, and eventual matched send-level outcome for every send.
